question.:question/problem: Given that $F=2\left(2x{y}^{2}\,i+4{x}^{2}y\,j\right),$ what is $\text{div}\,F?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=2\left(P\,i+Q\,j\right)$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
\text{div}\,F=∇\cdot F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}.
$$

  

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\left(2x{y}^{2}\right))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\left(4{x}^{2}y\right)) \\  & =2\left(2{y}^{2}+4{x}^{2}\right) \\  & =2\left(4{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the vector field $F=-3\left(x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,i+y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,j\right).$ 
Evaluate $∇\cdot F$ at the point $(3,4).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=-3\left(P\,i+Q\,j\right)$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
∇\cdot F=\text{div}\,F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}.
$$

  

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-3\left(x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\right))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-3\left(y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\right)) \\  & =-3\left(\frac{2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+\frac{{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\right) \\  & =-3\left(\frac{3{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\right) \\  & =-3\left(3\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\text{div}\,F$ at the point $(3,4),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\cdot F)(3,4) & =-3\left(3\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}}\right) \\  & =-3\left(3\sqrt{9+16}\right) \\  & =-3\left(3\sqrt{25}\right) \\  & =-3\left(15\right).\end{aligned}
$$
